beats.title: Comuneros Revolt in New Granada
beats.description: Thousands of townspeople marched on Bogota against crushing colonial taxes, forcing a short-lived settlement with Spanish officials.

beats.title: Inconfidencia Mineira Plot Exposed
beats.description: Brazilian miners, poets and a dentist nicknamed Tiradentes plotted to overthrow Portuguese rule before they were betrayed.

beats.title: Haitian Revolution Begins
beats.description: Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue rose in a vast uprising that launched a long revolution.
beats.why_in: start of Haiti's war of independence
beats.note: Began with the August uprising after the Bois Caiman ceremony

beats.title: Narino Prints the Rights of Man
beats.description: Antonio Narino secretly printed a Spanish translation of the French declaration of rights in Bogota and was later jailed for it.
beats.why_in: early independence ideas in New Granada
beats.note: Sources split between 1793 (printed, December) and 1794 (arrest); used 1793

beats.title: Gual and Espana Conspiracy
beats.description: A plot centred on the port of La Guaira sought a republic with equality among races and was crushed by Spanish authorities.

beats.title: Toussaint's Constitution for Haiti
beats.description: Toussaint Louverture had a constitution proclaimed that made him governor for life, without waiting for approval from Paris.

beats.title: Toussaint Louverture Is Captured
beats.description: French forces tricked and arrested the Haitian revolutionary leader and shipped him to a freezing fortress prison in France.

beats.title: Haiti Declares Independence
beats.description: Jean-Jacques Dessalines proclaimed a free nation, the first state in Latin America to break from European rule.

beats.title: Portuguese Court Lands in Brazil
beats.description: Chased by Napoleon's army, the royal family reached Rio de Janeiro, turning a colony into the seat of an empire.
beats.why_in: set Brazil on road to independence
beats.note: Fleet sailed late 1807; arrival in Brazil and Rio was 1808, used 1808

beats.title: Grito de Dolores
beats.description: A village priest named Miguel Hidalgo rang his church bell and called his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule in Mexico.
beats.why_in: start of Mexican War of Independence

beats.title: Venezuela Declares Independence
beats.description: A congress in Caracas adopted a declaration formally breaking with Spain and founding a republic that soon collapsed.

beats.title: Bolivar Named El Libertador
beats.description: After the Admirable Campaign retook Caracas, Simon Bolivar was hailed with the title that would define him.
beats.note: Entered Caracas August 1813; formal title ceremony October 1813; year agrees

beats.title: San Martin Crosses the Andes
beats.description: An army of Argentines and Chileans hauled artillery over high mountain passes to surprise the Spanish in Chile.
beats.why_in: campaign to free Chile and Peru

beats.title: Battle of Boyaca
beats.description: Bolivar's army surprised and defeated Spanish royalists in the Colombian highlands, opening the road to Bogota.

beats.title: Battle of Carabobo
beats.description: Bolivar's patriots defeated the royalist army near Valencia, securing the independence of Venezuela.
beats.note: Second battle of that name, not the 1814 one

beats.title: Cry of Ipiranga
beats.description: Prince Pedro drew his sword beside a Sao Paulo stream and declared Brazil separate from Portugal.

beats.title: Battle of Ayacucho
beats.description: Sucre's patriot army crushed the last major Spanish force in South America in the Peruvian highlands.
beats.why_in: ended Spanish rule on the continent

beats.title: Uruguay Becomes Independent
beats.description: A treaty brokered by Britain created a buffer state between Argentina and Brazil after a long struggle over the region.

beats.title: Bolivar Dies Near Santa Marta
beats.description: The Liberator died ill and embittered on the Colombian coast as his union of Venezuela, Colombia and Ecuador fell apart.

beats.title: Spain Recognizes Mexico
beats.description: Madrid finally signed a treaty accepting Mexican independence after years of refusing to acknowledge its loss.

beats.title: Duarte Founds La Trinitaria
beats.description: Juan Pablo Duarte formed a secret society in Santo Domingo to win independence from Haitian rule.

beats.title: Dominicans Declare Independence
beats.description: Rebels seized a city gate in Santo Domingo and proclaimed their separation from Haiti, founding a new republic.

beats.title: Narciso Lopez Invades Cuba
beats.description: A Venezuelan-born general led American volunteers to free Cuba from Spain but was captured and executed in Havana.

beats.title: Battle of Puebla
beats.description: Mexican defenders beat back a better-equipped French army, a victory still celebrated each May.
beats.why_in: defence of Mexican sovereignty against French invasion
beats.note: Borderline: defence of independence rather than break from Spain

beats.title: Dominicans Rise at Capotillo
beats.description: Patriots raised their flag at a hill on the Haitian border to drive out Spain, which had retaken the country.

beats.title: Spain Leaves Santo Domingo
beats.description: Spanish troops evacuated the Dominican Republic after a costly guerrilla war, ending the re-annexation.
beats.why_in: end of Spanish rule in Dominican Republic
beats.note: Month varies by source (May to July)

beats.title: Maximilian Executed in Mexico
beats.description: Mexican republicans shot the Austrian archduke installed as emperor by France, ending a European attempt to rule the country.

beats.title: Grito de Yara
beats.description: Carlos Manuel de Cespedes freed his slaves and declared war on Spain, opening Cuba's first long war for independence.
beats.why_in: start of Cuba's Ten Years' War

beats.title: The Virginius Affair
beats.description: Spain executed dozens aboard a ship carrying arms to Cuban rebels, nearly provoking war with the United States.

beats.title: Protest of Baragua
beats.description: General Antonio Maceo refused to accept the peace that ended the Ten Years' War, vowing to keep fighting for Cuba.

beats.title: Marti Founds Cuba's Rebel Party
beats.description: Jose Marti united exiles in a party to organize a new war for Cuban and Puerto Rican independence.

beats.title: Grito de Baire
beats.description: A fresh uprising began across eastern Cuba, and Jose Marti landed soon after, only to die in battle within weeks.
beats.why_in: start of Cuban War of Independence

beats.title: Antonio Maceo Killed in Action
beats.description: The Bronze Titan, Cuba's most feared rebel general, was killed near Havana, a heavy blow to the independence army.

beats.title: Puerto Rico Granted Autonomy
beats.description: Spain gave Puerto Rico a self-governing charter, too late to head off American intervention.
beats.why_in: Puerto Rico's path from Spanish rule

beats.title: Spain Loses Cuba and Puerto Rico
beats.description: After a brief war with the United States, Spain ceded its last major American colonies by treaty.
beats.why_in: end of Spanish rule in the Americas

beats.title: Cuba Becomes a Republic
beats.description: The American occupation ended and Tomas Estrada Palma took office as the first president of independent Cuba.
